root_cause.text: The `iommufd` selftest ioctl `IOMMU_TEST_OP_ADD_RESERVED` failed to validate the user-supplied reservation length, allowing `start + length - 1` to overflow in `iommufd_test_add_reserved()` and corrupt the `iopt` reserved interval tree.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (!length) return -EINVAL;` and `if (check_add_overflow(start, length - 1, &last)) return -EOVERFLOW;` before calling `iopt_reserve_iova()`, and the commit message says syzkaller could “overflow math in the test infrastructure and cause a WARN_ON by corrupting the reserved interval tree.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix reserved IOVA range handling by rejecting zero-length requests and preventing overflow when computing the end address.
intent_record.what: The function now declares a new local variable `last`, adds an early return of `-EINVAL` when `length` is zero, adds an overflow check using `check_add_overflow(start, length - 1, &last)` that returns `-EOVERFLOW` on failure, and changes the `iopt_reserve_iova()` call to pass `last` instead of computing `start + length - 1` inline.
intent_record.how: This prevents reservation requests with zero length from proceeding and avoids unsigned arithmetic overflow when calculating the end of the reserved IOVA range. At runtime, the code now rejects invalid inputs early and only reserves a valid, bounded range.

The vulnerable helper is `iommufd_test_add_reserved()`, which directly implements `IOMMU_TEST_OP_ADD_RESERVED`: `rc = iopt_reserve_iova(&ioas->iopt, start, start + length - 1, NULL);`.
